name: Cat in a Flat
tagline: Two-sided marketplace that matches cat owners with local cat sitters, with bookings, reviews and insurance attached.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Sitters set their own nightly or per-visit rates and the platform takes a booking fee, so there is no meaningful monthly number.

verdictSummary: The website is the easy part: profiles, a search map, a calendar, a messaging thread and a payment hold are all textbook CRUD plus Stripe. What you cannot generate is a few hundred vetted strangers within cycling distance of your flat who are willing to feed your cat next Thursday. Every piece of real value here lives on the other side of the account: supply density, reviews written by people who are not you, ID checks and the insurance cover that makes handing over your keys feel sane. A personal clone has exactly one sitter in it, which is called a contacts app. Build the logistics half if you already have sitters you trust, and keep the marketplace for finding new ones.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-household app that stores your trusted sitters, cat care instructions and booking history, and generates a printable handover sheet plus a visit log with photos.
requirements: Node 20 and a local machine or a cheap VPS
You already know at least one or two sitters personally
Optional: a mail or messaging channel you set up yourself for sending the handover sheet
whatYouLose: Supply: a searchable pool of nearby sitters you have never met
Trust signals: ID verification, background checks and reviews from other owners
Insurance and dispute handling if something goes wrong while you are away
Escrowed payment, so money and accountability are now a private arrangement
Last minute cover, which is the single reason most people open the app at all
moatNotes: Liquidity is hyperlocal here. The relevant market is not a country, it is a twenty minute walk from your door, which makes it much harder to bootstrap than a global marketplace.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the fee is not buying software, it is buying a shortlist of plausible strangers plus a reason to believe them. The booking fee covers vetting, cover for accidents and a payment flow that means nobody has to negotiate cash with someone holding their keys. Owners also pay for liquidity under pressure: the flight is tomorrow, the usual sitter is away, and only a populated marketplace solves that. Once a few good sitters are saved in the account, the platform is mostly habit and insurance, but that is enough.
notes: The booking app is a one sitting build; the sitters are not. The moat is hyperlocal supply density plus the vetting and insurance that make strangers with your keys an acceptable idea.
prompt:
Build a local, single-household cat care logistics app. This is NOT a marketplace: there is no sitter signup, no search, no payments, no discovery. It manages sitters I already know and trust.

Stack, no alternatives:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, schema created on first run
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, no auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud services

Data model:
- Cat: name, photo, age, vet name and phone, microchip id, medication notes, feeding schedule (free text plus times), litter notes, quirks, emergency contact
- Sitter: name, phone, email, how I know them, rate per visit, notes, trusted flag
- Booking: sitter, date range, visits per day, agreed rate, status (draft, confirmed, done), total computed from visits and rate
- Visit: belongs to a booking, timestamp, free text log, optional photo upload stored under ./uploads

Screens:
1. Dashboard: next booking, countdown, quick link to the handover sheet
2. Cats: list and edit form
3. Sitters: list and edit form
4. Bookings: list, create form with a date range picker, detail page showing the visit log
5. Handover sheet: a print-optimised page per booking that merges cat details, feeding schedule, vet info and door or key instructions into something I can print or save as PDF with the browser
6. Visit log entry: a deliberately mobile-friendly page at /booking/[id]/log that a sitter can open from a link on their phone to add a note and a photo, no login, access by unguessable booking token

Explicitly out of scope: sitter discovery, reviews, ratings, payments, insurance, push notifications, email sending, multi-user accounts.

Secrets, if any are ever needed, go in .env and .env.example. Seed the database with one example cat, one sitter and one past booking so the UI is not empty on first run. Write a short README explaining the token-link behaviour and that this thing is meant to run on my own machine or a private VPS only.
